npcs.name: Okan-Zeeus, Hist-Tender
npcs.greet: The Hist of Okeeh drinks slowly this season, and so do I. Forgive an old tender. My roots are in two places today.

npcs.name: Seeks-Tomorrow
npcs.greet: Cloth, rope, Cyrodilic nails. I sell what the marsh cannot grow. Tomorrow I will sell more of it.

npcs.name: Livia Corvane
npcs.greet: The Legion left Stormhold. I did not. Someone has to write down the glyphs before the moss eats them.

npcs.name: Elder Hulum-Ei
npcs.greet: Warm-blood. You smell of roads. Sit downwind of me and we will both be happier.

npcs.name: Hatch-Mother Esh-Teeka
npcs.greet: Mind your boots near the warm-mud. Every pool you see has someone in it who has not been named yet.

npcs.name: Little Wiz-Tul
npcs.greet: Hatch-Mother says I talk too much for someone with no name-scales yet. I say she listens too little.

npcs.name: Junal-Lei, Ledger-Keeper
npcs.greet: Tariffs, tithes and births. If it happens in Stormhold, I have a column for it.

npcs.name: Many-Notches
npcs.greet: Count them if you like. One notch for every beast that tried to swallow me. The tail has run out of room.

npcs.name: Wanes-in-Shallows
npcs.greet: The fish are where they always were. It is the fishers who are missing.

npcs.name: Jee-Tazei, Harbor-Warden
npcs.greet: Every hull that ties up in Lilmoth pays a little, and every hull is a little heavier for it. That is my gift to the city.

npcs.name: Heem-Ra Tullus
npcs.greet: Boil your water. Wash your hands. I will say it to the King himself if he comes in coughing.

npcs.name: Tree-Speaker Asheel
npcs.greet: The city coughs and the Lukiul hand out boiled water. The Hist has better medicine, if anyone would ask it.

npcs.name: Reezal-Jul, Root-Speaker
npcs.greet: Murkmire is small, and the roots here are old. They notice when a stranger walks on them.

npcs.name: Decimus Tsleel
npcs.greet: Decimus, yes. My egg-name is longer and harder to fit on a ledger. Are you buying, or are you staring?

npcs.name: Old Xil-Mareeh
npcs.greet: My nephew wears trousers and an Imperial name. I still love him. It takes effort.

npcs.name: Flavia Fennic
npcs.greet: My family has kept a candle for the Ninth since before I was born. You are not here to sell me another, I hope.

npcs.name: Egg-Speaker Hixil
npcs.greet: The Tsleeksh lay their eggs in this sand every spring. Every spring, some are gone by morning. Walk carefully.

relics.name: Bloodied Tap-Spike
relics.desc: A copper spike for drawing sap, crusted amber. Someone filed a maker's mark off it in a hurry.

relics.name: Sap-Runner's Ledger
relics.desc: Casks, dates and a buyer in Bravil. The supplier is written only as 'the one with the copper earring'.

relics.name: Charcoal Glyph Rubbing
relics.desc: A rubbing of a leaning stone. The glyphs count seasons, then stop counting.

relics.name: Ukalith Calendar Stone
relics.desc: A wheel of green stone carved with the turning of the marsh. It is warm, as if something inside it is still keeping time.

relics.name: Purse of Harbor Silver
relics.desc: Imperial coin stamped with the Lilmoth harbor-tax mark, found in a Naga raider's bedroll.

relics.name: Indenture Papers
relics.desc: Imperial labor contracts for nine 'orphaned hatchlings', countersigned with a Stormhold ledger-seal.

relics.name: Flask of Cistern Water
relics.desc: Cloudy water from the Saltmouth Cisterns. It smells faintly of low tide and lamp oil.

relics.name: Coral Idol of Thras
relics.desc: A squat coral figure, slick to the touch, carved with too many arms. It is hollow, and someone has filled it with powdered bone.

relics.name: Leviathan Tooth
relics.desc: As long as a forearm and yellow as old sap. Many-Notches will want it for his tail.

relics.name: Bundle of Bones
relics.desc: The bones of an old Saxhleel trader, wrapped in waxed cloth and tied with a rope of green reed.

relics.name: Tarnished Eagle of the Ninth
relics.desc: A Legion standard-top, green with corrosion. The eagle has been bent, deliberately, until its wings touch.

relics.name: Stone Egg of the Xhuul
relics.desc: An egg-shaped river stone painted with a tribe's marks, old as the hatching-sands. Somebody stole it long ago.

relics.name: Censer of Unquiet Sleep
relics.desc: A black iron censer that still smells of poppy and burnt hair. Holding it makes your eyelids heavy.

relics.name: Ebonroot Orders
relics.desc: Orders in a Dunmer hand: salt the roots of the Helstrom Hist before the rains. Sealed with an ash-yam crest.

side_bm_okeeh_speaks: Amber weeps from a dozen small holes in the bark. The leaves above are the colour of old bruises.
Thin. Thin. A mouth on every root and none of them ours. Find the hands, warm-blood. The hands know the names.
side_bm_okeeh_heals: The holes in the bark close slowly, like eyes. Somewhere in the grove a frog begins to sing, then another.
The roots remember who bled them. The roots remember who stopped it.
side_bm_ukalith_wakes: The stair goes down further than the mound is tall. The air smells of resin and wet stone, and of something that has been asleep for a long time.
Count with me. Wet season. Dry season. Wet season. You are the first season in four thousand that walked in on two legs.
side_bm_ukalith_falls: Fool. The stone was not my treasure. It was my chain. Keep it turning, or the marsh forgets what year it is.
The embalmed priest folds into his robes like a dry leaf. The calendar stone ticks once in your hands, then again.
side_bm_coral_speaks: A voice bubbles out of the hold, thick and patient, as if spoken through a mouthful of water.
Little cough-city. Little cough-children. All so tender. My Voice has been very good to me. Come down and meet him.
side_bm_coral_unmasked: Behind a curtain of rotting sailcloth sits a speaking-tube of brass, and beneath it a cask with a bladder sewn to its lid.
There was never a Sload aboard. Only a Dunmer with a good imagination, and a great many frightened acolytes who never thought to look.
side_bm_ninth_muster: Ninth Legion, Second Cohort, present. Nobody relieved us. Nobody relieved us. We kept the gate.
The lizards came up out of the water and drowned my men. Honour us, citizen. Carry the eagle home and tell Gideon how we died.
side_bm_ninth_truth: Under the flooded cells the walls are scratched with tally marks. Hundreds of them, all made by clawed hands.
He opened the sluices when the rebellion came. The prisoners were in the lower cells. We heard them. We heard them until the water reached the ceiling.
side_bm_mourner_speaks: A pale light hangs over the pool, shaped like a crouching mother with her arms around nothing.
They took my clutch-stone. Tsleeksh hands, Tsleeksh grandfathers. I take one egg every spring. I will take them until the stone comes home.
side_bm_dream_hollow: The hollow is full of sleepers lying in the mud in a circle, breathing together. Their eyelids flicker.
Every hatchling in Stormhold dreams of me now. Such small dreams, such easy doors. Lie down with them, walker. It is warm.
side_bm_ebonroot_found: Barrels of rock salt are stacked to the rafters, each stamped with the same ash-yam crest. Enough to kill every root for a mile.
Some of the Dunmer here have not yet heard that the war is over. Some of them have, and do not care.

quests.title: The Bitter Sap
quests.offer: You look tired, tender. Is it the Hist?
quests.pitch: The Okeeh Hist is sick. Its leaves curl, its sap runs bitter, and the hatchlings of Helstrom wake from its dreams crying. The young ones say a Sload has cursed it. I say a curse does not leave footprints. Go and look at it with warm-blood eyes.
quests.desc: Okan-Zeeus, Hist-tender of Helstrom, asked me to find out why the Okeeh Hist is sickening. The town blames a curse; he does not.

objectives.text: Visit the Okeeh-Hist Grove
Pull the tap-spike from the Hist's root
objectives.journal: Someone had been tapping the Hist in the dark, a little from each root so nobody would notice. Not a curse. A harvest.

objectives.text: Follow the drag-marks to the river landing
Drive off the sap-runners' crew
Kill Gallus Vend, master of the sap-runners
objectives.journal: Vend was loading casks of Hist sap for Bravil, where alchemists pay in gold for one drop. His ledger names a local supplier only by a copper earring.

objectives.text: Find the trader with the copper earring in Helstrom
objectives.topic: You wear a copper earring, Seeks-Tomorrow. So does the name in Gallus Vend's ledger.
objectives.reply: So. The tree has a long memory and you have a short road. I wanted a warehouse, a ship, a life that is not mud. The Hist was dying anyway, I told myself. It was not. I made it so.

choices.label: Okan-Zeeus will decide what happens to you.
choices.reply: Then I will go to him with my head down. He is my hatch-brother, you know. That is the worst of it.

choices.label: Pay back the Hist. Tend its roots every dry season until it forgives you.
choices.reply: Every dry season? That is a long sentence for a short-lived merchant. ...Yes. I will carry the water. Thank you.

objectives.text: Bring the ledger to Okan-Zeeus
objectives.topic: There was no curse. Only hands, and a ledger.
objectives.reply: Seeks-Tomorrow. I knew before you said it; I smelled the sap on her hands at the last naming-day and told myself it was a gift. The Hist will mend. Take what grew in the bark while it slept. It wanted you to have it.

quests.outro: The Okeeh Hist was not cursed but bled for Cyrodilic coin, and the hand on the spike belonged to its own tender's hatch-sister. The grove is singing again.

quests.title: The Ukalith Calendar
quests.pitch: Glyph-stones from the far north of Shadowfen. They lean toward one mound, all of them, like signposts. My books say a Xanmeer lies under it, buried in mud for longer than the Empire has had a name. I cannot dig it myself. My knees are Imperial and so is my courage.
quests.desc: Livia Corvane, an Imperial antiquarian who stayed in Stormhold after the Legion left, wants me to follow a line of leaning glyph-stones to a buried Xanmeer in northern Shadowfen.

objectives.text: Find the leaning glyph-stones in Shadowfen
Take a rubbing of the last stone
Find the buried Xanmeer the stones point toward
Destroy the root-wardens in the stepped halls
Defeat Ixtaxh the Sap-Embalmed
Lift the calendar stone from its socket
objectives.journal: The guardian said the stone was his chain, not his treasure. It ticks when I hold it, like a heart that keeps the seasons.

objectives.text: Ask Elder Hulum-Ei what the stone is
objectives.topic: This stone came out of a Xanmeer in Shadowfen. It keeps time.
objectives.reply: It keeps the marsh's time, which is not yours. Our oldest priests turned stones like this to tell the Hist when to wake. It does not belong in a glass case in the Imperial City. But you carried it. You choose.

objectives.text: Give the calendar stone to Livia or to Elder Hulum-Ei
objectives.topic: Here is the calendar stone of Ukalith.
objectives.reply: Then it is decided, and it is done. Whatever happens to the seasons now, at least someone will be watching them.

quests.outro: I woke the warden of Xanmeer Ukalith and carried away the calendar stone he was bound to keep. Whoever holds it now holds the count of the marsh's seasons.

quests.title: Teeth on the Tide
quests.pitch: Naga. They come up from the south in long boats with their jaws painted red, and they take nets, smoked fish, sometimes the fishers too. They used to raid once a generation. Now it is every new moon. Somebody is feeding them, and it is not the river.
quests.desc: Wanes-in-Shallows of Murkmire says Naga raiders have been striking the fishing stilts every new moon. She thinks someone is paying them.

objectives.text: Beat back the Naga raid on the Murkmire stilts
Follow the raiders' boats to their tide camp near Lilmoth
Clear the Naga tide camp
Kill Kallax Jaw-Wide
Search Kallax's bedroll
objectives.journal: Kallax slept on a purse of new Imperial coin stamped with the Lilmoth harbor-tax mark. Whoever pays the Naga collects the harbor tax.

objectives.text: Confront the Harbor-Warden of Lilmoth
objectives.topic: Your tax-silver was in a Naga raidmaster's bed, Jee-Tazei.
objectives.reply: Then the raidmaster was a thief as well as a cutthroat. ...No. You have the look of someone who already knows. Empty stilts sell cheap. I meant to buy the whole shore and build a proper harbor where Murkmire stands. It would have been good for everyone. Later.

choices.label: You will repay every family in Murkmire. Twice over.
choices.reply: Twice. Yes. The harbor will wait another lifetime. Go before I change my mind about being sorry.

choices.label: The King will hear of this.
choices.reply: The King hears many things. But he will hear this one from you, so I suppose it will stick.

objectives.text: Bring the harbor silver back to Wanes-in-Shallows
objectives.topic: The raids are over. This is what paid for them.
objectives.reply: A harbor-warden. Of course. The Naga only bite; it takes a city to chew. We will buy new nets with his silver. It is the only sweet thing about it.

quests.outro: The Naga raids on Murkmire were bought and paid for by Lilmoth's own harbor-warden, who wanted the shore empty. Kallax Jaw-Wide will not paint his jaws again.

quests.title: Chains in the Reeds
quests.offer: Why are the hatchery pools guarded?
quests.pitch: Because nine are missing. Not eggs; hatchlings, small ones, with no names yet. A boat came up the channel at night with a lamp shuttered. The Lukiul clerks say the children wandered. Hatchlings do not wander nine at a time.
quests.desc: Hatch-Mother Esh-Teeka told me nine nameless hatchlings vanished from the Warm-Mud Hatchery outside Stormhold. A shuttered boat was seen in the channel.

objectives.text: Search the Warm-Mud Hatchery for signs of the boat
Kill the slavers who came back for more
objectives.journal: The men who came back for a second boatload wore old Legion tunics with the badges cut off. One of them carried a contract with a Stormhold seal.

objectives.text: Follow the boat west to the Reedwall Stockade
Break the stockade's guard
Kill Overseer Septimus Crane
objectives.journal: Crane meant to sell the hatchlings to plantations along the Niben as 'indentured orphans'. His papers were in perfect order. That was the most frightening thing about them.

objectives.text: Lead Little Wiz-Tul and the hatchlings home to the hatchery
Ask Junal-Lei about the seal on the papers
objectives.topic: These indentures carry your ledger-seal, Junal-Lei.
objectives.reply: They carry the seal for orphans. Crane brought me a list of orphans and coin for the filing fee, and I filed. I did not look at the pools. I looked at the column. Gods of every land, I looked at the column.

choices.label: You will stand in front of the hatchery and tell every mother what you did.
choices.reply: Every mother. Yes. I will learn the names of the nine, too. All of them.

choices.label: Burn the papers and say nothing. Crane is dead.
choices.reply: That is kind, and it is wrong, and I will take it. I will never seal another page without reading it. Never.

objectives.text: Give the indenture papers to Esh-Teeka
objectives.topic: The nine are home. These are the papers that sold them.
objectives.reply: I will hang them over the warm-mud so the hatchlings learn what ink can do. You walk like a Shadowscale, warm-blood. Take this. It was left with us by one, long ago, for a day like today.

quests.outro: Nine hatchlings came home to the Warm-Mud Hatchery. The Imperial overseer who bought them is dead, and the ledger that made it lawful has been read aloud.

quests.title: The Grey Cough
quests.pitch: Half the lower city. Grey phlegm, grey scales, then a fever that boils the eyes. Tree-Speaker Asheel says the Hist is punishing Lukiul like me for drinking boiled water. I say something is in the water. Help me prove one of us right before we both run out of patients.
quests.desc: Heem-Ra Tullus, a Lukiul healer in Lilmoth, believes the grey cough sweeping the lower city comes from the water. The traditional Tree-Speaker blames the city's neglect of the Hist.

objectives.text: Hear Tree-Speaker Asheel's side
objectives.topic: Heem-Ra says the cough comes from the water.
objectives.reply: Heem-Ra is clever and loud, which is a dangerous mix. The Hist showed me a dream: a soft grey mouth drinking from the city's cisterns. Water, yes. But not the kind you boil.

objectives.text: Go to the Saltmouth Cisterns north of Lilmoth
Destroy the things nesting in the cisterns
Fill a flask from the poisoned cistern
objectives.journal: The cisterns were full of drowned dead dumped in from a barge, and a smear of grey slime on every stone. Both healers were half right.

objectives.text: Bring the cistern water to Heem-Ra
objectives.topic: The cisterns are full of corpses and grey slime.
objectives.reply: Corpses dumped where the city drinks. That is not sickness, that is a sermon. Someone wants Lilmoth weak and frightened. Asheel's dream said a grey mouth; tell her she was right, and tell her I said so. It will choke me less than this cough.

objectives.text: Tell Asheel what the cisterns held
objectives.topic: Heem-Ra says you were right. The grey mouth is real.
objectives.reply: She said that? Aloud? ...Then the Hist and the kettle agree for once. The barge that fed the cisterns is moored east of the city. The fishers call it the Coral Promise and will not go near it.

quests.outro: The grey cough came from corpses tipped into the Saltmouth Cisterns. Lilmoth's healer and its Tree-Speaker agreed on something, which the city may remember longer than the plague.

quests.title: The Voice of Thras
quests.desc: The barge that poisoned Lilmoth's cisterns is moored east of the city. The fishers say a Sload speaks from its hold.

objectives.text: Ask Reezal-Jul in Murkmire about the Coral Promise
objectives.topic: What do you know of a barge called the Coral Promise?
objectives.reply: The roots here felt it pass. Cold, like a drowned thing. Murkmire's dead went missing from the mud-graves last season, and their wraps were found floating near Lilmoth. Thras is far away. Its servants are not.

objectives.text: Board the Hulk of the Coral Promise
Cut through the barge's acolytes and their dead
Kill Orvas Ilmeth, the Voice of Thras
Take the coral idol from the hold
objectives.journal: The Sload in the hold was a speaking-tube and a wet bladder. Orvas Ilmeth needed a master more frightening than himself to keep his acolytes obedient. His plague, at least, was real.

objectives.text: Bring the idol to Reezal-Jul
objectives.topic: There was no Sload. Only a Dunmer and a speaking-tube.
objectives.reply: Ha. A false god with a real plague. That is the Sload way, even without the Sload. I will sink this idol in the deep mud where the roots can grind it. Murkmire's dead will come home to the graves.

quests.outro: The Voice of Thras was a Dunmer necromancer pretending to speak for a Sload. He is dead, the barge is empty, and Murkmire's stolen dead have been put back in the mud.

quests.title: Mother of Floods
quests.offer: Is there room on your tail for one more notch?
quests.pitch: One more, yes. A wamasu up in Shadowfen, as long as three boats and fat with lightning. It took two of my hunters at the Low-Water Mere. I want its belly-stone. You want a story to tell. We meet at the stilt-camp.
quests.desc: Many-Notches, a tail-hunter of Stormhold, wants help killing a giant wamasu that ate two of his hunters at the Low-Water Mere in Shadowfen.

objectives.text: Meet the tail-hunters at their stilt-camp in Shadowfen
Drive the hackwings off the hunters' smoking-racks
Wade into the Low-Water Mere
Kill Storm-Gut the wamasu
objectives.journal: Storm-Gut died spitting lightning. Then the whole mere bulged upward. The wamasu had not been eating the hunters. It had been running from something bigger.

objectives.text: Wait for the leviathan to surface after dark
Kill the Mother-of-Floods
Bring the leviathan's tooth to Many-Notches in Stormhold
objectives.topic: The wamasu was the small one.
objectives.reply: A leviathan. In the Mere. I have hunted those waters thirty years and called them shallow. ...I will not cut a notch for this one. I will cut a new tail. Here; you have earned the hunter's share and more.

quests.outro: The wamasu Many-Notches hired me to kill was fleeing a swamp leviathan, the Mother-of-Floods. Both are dead, and the Low-Water Mere is merely deep again.

quests.title: Two Names for One Father
quests.offer: You look like a man between two funerals.
quests.pitch: Exactly between them. My father died last month. I paid for an Imperial tomb, a good one, with his name in marble. My aunt says his bones belong to the Sedge-Root Hist, the old way, to be drunk back into the tree. Now his bones are missing from the Hist altogether, and she says I stole them. I did not. Find them, please, before this family eats itself.
quests.desc: Decimus Tsleel, a Lukiul trader of Gideon, wants his late father's bones found. His traditional aunt laid them at the Sedge-Root Hist; now they are gone, and each blames the other.

objectives.text: Speak with Old Xil-Mareeh
objectives.topic: Decimus says he did not take his father's bones.
objectives.reply: Then he has learned to lie as well as he has learned to wear shoes. ...No. You believe him. Go to the Sedge-Root and look for yourself. The Hist does not lie, even when nephews do.

objectives.text: Visit the Sedge-Root Hist outside Gideon
Kill the troll gnawing on the burial-mound
objectives.journal: Neither of them took the bones. A troll had been digging up the burial-mound for marrow. I nearly laughed, and then I saw what it had been chewing.

objectives.text: Gather the old trader's bones
Return to Decimus with the bones
objectives.topic: A troll took them, not your aunt. Where should they rest?
objectives.reply: A troll. All that shouting, and a troll. You decide. I cannot, and if Aunt Xil decides, I will hear about it for the rest of my life.

choices.label: Give them back to the Hist, the old way.
choices.reply: The old way. He would have laughed at the tomb anyway; he hated marble. Take them to my aunt. Tell her I said yes before she can ask.

choices.label: Bury them in the tomb, with his trade-name in marble.
choices.reply: Then he will have both names, one in stone and one in her stories. Take them to Aunt Xil first. She should be the one to carry them in.

objectives.text: Bring the bones to Old Xil-Mareeh
objectives.topic: Your nephew sends these, and his apology.
objectives.reply: His apology. Hm. Two words from a Lukiul, and both of them mine. ...Thank you, warm-blood. The family will argue about something else now. That is how you know it is healed.

quests.outro: Decimus Tsleel's father's bones were stolen by a troll, not by family. The Lukiul trader and his traditional aunt chose a resting place together.

quests.title: The Ninth at Mirefast

find.text: A Legion grave marker sunk to its shoulders in the mud. Scratched beneath the name, fresher than the rest: 'Ninth, Second Cohort. Still at Mirefast. Still waiting to be relieved.'

quests.desc: Outside Gideon I found a Legion grave scratched with a plea from the Ninth Legion's Second Cohort, who never left Mirefast Penitentiary.

objectives.text: Find Mirefast Penitentiary in the western marsh
Lay the restless garrison of Mirefast to rest
Search the flooded lower cells
objectives.journal: The Prefect said Argonians drowned his men. The scratch-marks in the lower cells tell it the other way round: he opened the sluices on his own prisoners and drowned them in their cells.

objectives.text: Destroy the ghost of Prefect Aulus Fennic
Take the bent eagle of the Ninth
Find the Prefect's descendant in Gideon
objectives.topic: I found your ancestor at Mirefast.
objectives.reply: Prefect Aulus Fennic. We are taught he held Mirefast against the rebellion and died with his cohort. Is that what you found?

choices.label: He drowned his prisoners and lied about it for two hundred years.
choices.reply: ...Then the candle was for the wrong dead. I will put out his, and light theirs. Someone in this family should have asked sooner.

choices.label: He died at his post. His men waited for him to the end.
choices.reply: That is what we always believed. Thank you. I will keep the candle burning for the Ninth.

objectives.text: Give Flavia the eagle of the Ninth
objectives.topic: This was theirs. The men who waited.
objectives.reply: Bent wings. Someone did that on purpose. I think I understand why, now. Take this, from the family chest. It belonged to an honest soldier of the Ninth, which turns out to be rarer than we were told.

quests.outro: The ghosts of the Ninth Legion's Second Cohort are at rest. Their Prefect drowned his prisoners at Mirefast and lied about it in death as he had in life.

quests.title: The Stone Egg
quests.pitch: We say a curse. Every spring one clutch is empty by morning, no tracks, no broken shells. The Tsleeksh have lived with it for nine generations. My hatchlings are now the age when we start to lay. I would like them to live without it.
quests.desc: Egg-Speaker Hixil of the Tsleeksh tribe asked me to break a curse that has stolen one clutch of eggs every spring for nine generations.

objectives.text: Keep watch over the hatching-sands by night
Drive off the wisps drifting over the sand
objectives.journal: Pale lights came to the sands at midnight and drifted north with something cradled between them. I followed.

objectives.text: Follow the lights to the Mourning Pool
Ask Hixil about the clutch-stone
objectives.topic: The ghost at the pool says the Tsleeksh stole her clutch-stone.
objectives.reply: ...The stone egg. It sits in our naming-hut. My grandmothers called it a gift from the Xhuul, a tribe that died out. Died out, they said. I have never asked how. I am asking now, and I do not like the answer.

objectives.text: Face the Hatch-Mourner at the pool
objectives.journal: The Mourner would not hear me until she was spent. When the light went out of her, she was only a tired mother looking at a stone.

objectives.text: Sink the stone egg into the Mourning Pool and keep vigil
Tell Egg-Speaker Hixil it is done
objectives.topic: The Xhuul stone is home. The Mourner is quiet.
objectives.reply: Nine generations of empty nests for one stolen stone. The Hist teaches that everything returns to the roots eventually. It did not say how long the roots would wait. Thank you, warm-blood. The Tsleeksh owe you a name. We will think of a good one.

quests.outro: The Tsleeksh curse was a mother's ghost whose clutch-stone they had stolen long ago. The stone is back in the Mourning Pool and the hatching-sands are quiet.

quests.title: Small Dreams, Easy Doors

find.text: A black altar crusted with poppy-wax. Tucked under the candles is a hatchling's moss-doll, and a note in a clawed hand: 'Every one of them sleeps in my hollow now. East. Bring more.'

quests.desc: Near Vaermina's shrine in Shadowfen I found an altar holding a hatchling's doll and a note boasting of dreamers kept in a hollow to the east.

objectives.text: Find the hollow east of Vaermina's shrine
Kill the sleepwalkers guarding the circle
Wake up, and kill Drinks-Sleep
objectives.journal: Drinks-Sleep had been reaching into the dreams of Stormhold's hatchlings through this censer, using their small minds as doors for Vaermina. The sleepers in the circle woke when he died, crying for water.

objectives.text: Warn Hatch-Mother Esh-Teeka in Stormhold
objectives.topic: Have the hatchlings been dreaming of a stranger?
objectives.reply: A smiling man in a hollow. All of them, for a month. We thought it was the Hist teaching them fear. It was not the Hist. ...Last night, for the first time, they slept without crying.

objectives.text: Give the censer to Esh-Teeka to be drowned
objectives.topic: This was his door. Sink it somewhere deep.
objectives.reply: In the warm-mud, where only the newest hatch. Let it learn what it is to be small and not dream at all.

quests.outro: A Vaermina cultist called Drinks-Sleep was using the dreams of Stormhold's hatchlings as doors. His censer is under the warm-mud and the children sleep quietly.

quests.title: Salt for the Roots

find.text: A Dunmer courier's bones in a ruined chitin cuirass. His satchel is still sealed: an order to 'hold Ebonroot until the rains', and a crude map to an old fort in the northern fens.

quests.desc: Near Helstrom I found a dead Dunmer courier carrying orders for a garrison at a fort called Ebonroot, in the northern fens of Shadowfen.

objectives.text: Find Fort Ebonroot in northern Shadowfen
Fight through the Dunmer holdouts
Seize the garrison's sealed orders
objectives.journal: The orders were to salt the roots of the Helstrom Hist before the rains. Captain Sadri came for me before I could finish reading them.

objectives.text: Hurry to the Okeeh-Hist Grove before the rains
Stop the salters at the Hist's roots
Show the orders to Okan-Zeeus
objectives.topic: A Dunmer garrison meant to salt the Okeeh roots.
objectives.reply: Salt. Not fire, not axes. Salt, so that nothing would grow for a hundred years. Some old wars do not know how to die. Thank you, warm-blood. Twice now the Okeeh has you to thank, or once, if you came here first.

quests.outro: A forgotten Dunmer garrison at Fort Ebonroot planned to salt the roots of Helstrom's Hist. Their captain is dead and the salt is in the river.
